definition: The Pile is an 886 GB diverse, open-source dataset of English text created to train large language models (LLMs).
details: It was constructed by EleutherAI in 2020 and publicly released on December 31 of that year. It is composed of 22 sub-datasets, including books, movie transcripts, and scientific papers, among other media. The Pile and Common Crawl had been, as of 2024, the two main training datasets being used to train AI models. Copyright disputes centering around use of The Pile escalated in 2023, prompting Eleuther to start removing some datasets. Eleuther partnered with various organizations to release Common Pile v0.1 in 2025 in order to have a large curated training dataset without the copyright issues.

explainer.lead: The Pile is an 886 GB open-source English text dataset built to train large language models. Its breadth made it one of the two main training datasets used for AI models as of 2024, and it became a focus of copyright disputes.

tiers.eli5: Think of it as a giant library assembled from 22 smaller collections—books, movie transcripts, scientific papers—so a model can read widely before learning to write.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a large, diverse pretraining corpus with clearly separated sub-datasets, which makes it easy to ablate or drop sources. A pitfall is that individual sub-datasets were removed over time amid copyright disputes, so reproductions can drift from the original composition.
tiers.paperLevel: A 886 GB dataset of English text composed of 22 sub-datasets, constructed by EleutherAI in 2020 and released December 31, 2020. Its known limit is that it is English-only and that its contents have been partially removed, so it is not a fixed artifact.

explainer.example: A team pretraining a language model might sample mainly from the books and scientific-paper sub-datasets, then hold out others to test how each source affects downstream performance.
